recent_status_events.author: claude
recent_status_events.counterevidence_considered: The count is still a floor: six deals met the rule without a citable page, and acquihires surface late, so later searches can add deals to quarters already read. The rise from 23 to 39 is mostly 2025's slow start leaving the window; the quarters of 2026 held about a dozen deals each. The dead band is now seven deals, about the spread between two years' counts with no trend.
recent_status_events.reason: The ledger was searched on 23 Sep 2026 under a rule written down first, for all 120 counted buyers from January 2025: it gained 43 deals and lost two that fall outside its scope (TBPN, a media company, and DuckLabs, a database maker). The count now reads 23 at 31 Dec 2025, 34 at 31 Mar 2026 and 39 at 30 Jun 2026. The direction rule compares five quarters a search has covered, so it cannot be read until the search after the end of 2026.

recent_status_events.author: claude
recent_status_events.counterevidence_considered: Occupational mix moves slowly by construction, and a CPS-based index cannot see task change within an occupation. The index between recent and older graduates read above 33 from March to August 2026, its longest run above that line since 2021, which the Lab's September update does not read as disruption.
recent_status_events.reason: The index now comes from the chart data of the Budget Lab's AI labour-market tracker, current to August 2026: 5.50 pp forty-five months after November 2022, inside the normal band (7.5 pp or less), against 5.17 pp for the January 2021 baseline at the same age. The event before cited the March 2026 row of the Lab's workbook, which the tracker's data revise from 5.26 to 5.256.

recent_status_events.author: claude
recent_status_events.counterevidence_considered: April read 51.0% on the same monthly series, so both monthly readings sit just above the edge; the weekly readings of 53.3% and 54.5% came from seven-day samples of Claude.ai conversations, so the step between them cannot be read as a trend. One provider's consumer plans, classified by a model.
recent_status_events.reason: The Economic Index's monthly readings now sit on a series of their own: from its June 2026 release the dataset samples Claude chat and Cowork conversations every day and reports them by calendar month, where earlier releases drew one seven-day sample of Claude.ai conversations, so the two are no longer drawn as one line. The reading is unchanged: augmentation is 51.4% of classified conversations in May 2026, within 5% of the normal band's edge at 50%, so the band-edge rule still holds the status at emerging.

verdict: As of 2026-09-22: compute & physical mixed, model mixed, training input emerging, serving & orchestration unmeasured, deployment & application dispersing (one reading), adopters (no capture rule yet), labour & consumers dispersing (one reading).
what_would_change: Rent concentration in semiconductors: Four fiscal quarters; a move under one point of margin is noise. Rising margin = rent concentrating at the chip layer.
Cloud backlog (remaining performance obligations): Four quarters; moves under $10B are noise at this scale. Growing backlog concentrates future cloud revenue in a few contracts.
Frontier-lab revenue run-rates: Four reports; moves under $2B are reporting noise. Rising run-rate concentrates revenue at the two frontier labs.
Lab recoupment ratio: Three points; a move under 0.05 is noise. A rising ratio means the lab is recouping capital faster than it raises it.

Consumer surplus from generative AI (willingness to accept): Two annual waves so far, so the trend is one step; moves under $10B are within survey error. Rising surplus disperses value away from producers to consumers.

Application layer's share of enterprise generative-AI spend (Menlo): Two annual waves, so the trend is one step; a move under five points is within survey error. Rising application share = value concentrating at the application layer.

Semiconductors' share of stack operating income: Four calendar quarters; a move under two points is within fiscal-calendar noise. Rising semis share = rent concentrating at the chip layer; falling = migrating up.

Chips' share of the stack's gross profit: Four calendar quarters, the same rule as the operating-income stack; a move under two points is fiscal-calendar noise. Rising = profit concentrating at the chip layer; falling = migrating up the stack.
Cloud segment operating margins: Four fiscal quarters; two points of margin is noise. Rising cloud margin under rising capex means the layer is keeping surplus.

Circular financing scale: Three quarters of the trailing-year flow; moves under $20B are one small deal. Rising commitments concentrate the stack's financing on a few counterparties, and unlike the cumulative total this series can fall.
Concentration among covered chip filers (HHI): Four calendar quarters; a move under 200 HHI points is noise. Rising = the covered chip layer concentrating further.
Concentration among covered cloud filers (HHI): Four calendar quarters; a move under 200 HHI points is noise.
Lab concentration of routed tokens (OpenRouter, HHI): Four weekly readings; under 0.02 in the index is table churn. Rising = routed tokens concentrating on fewer labs.

Price per unit of capability (cheapest METR-hour on OpenRouter): Four price change-points; a move under two cents per million tokens per horizon-hour is noise. Rising = labs keeping the surplus from capability gains.

Price per unit of capability (cheapest near-frontier model, Artificial Analysis): Four price change-points; a move under $0.0006 per million tokens per index point (about a tenth of the 11 Sep 2026 level) is one model's repricing. Rising = labs keeping the surplus from capability gains.
Frontier labs' share of tracked venture dollars: Four quarters; a move under five points is a single round's timing. Rising = capital concentrating in the frontier labs.
Vertical versus horizontal application funding: Four quarters; a move under 0.2x is round timing. Rising = capital concentrating in vertical applications.
Frontier lab valuation to run-rate multiple: Three valuation events; a move under 3x is noise in press-reported run-rates. Rising = the market pricing more durable rents into the labs.

Lab vertical integration (acquisitions and acquihires, trailing four quarters): Four quarters. A yearly count of rare events varies between two years with no trend by about the square root of twice its level, which at the December 2025 count after the September 2026 search is about seven, so a smaller move is stable. More deals per year concentrate the application layer into the labs.

Open-weights gap to the closed frontier (ECI points): Four open-weights releases; a move under two ECI points is inside the index's confidence intervals. Widening gap = rents concentrating in the closed labs.
Non-Nvidia share of AI compute shipped (H100-equivalents): Four quarters; under two points is inside Epoch's estimate ranges. Rising non-Nvidia share = the chip layer's rent dispersing.

Hyperscaler capex to AI revenue (trailing year): Four quarters; a move under 0.3x is run-rate noise. Rising = capex pulling further ahead of revenue (the bet growing); falling = revenue catching the buildout.

Hyperscaler server useful lives (10-K estimates): Two annual readings; a change under half a year is rounding. A shorter life means faster hardware turnover and thinner margins for the layer, so shortening reads as dispersing.
Neocloud borrowing cost (CoreWeave facility rates): Three quarter-ends; moves under a percentage point are facility mix. Rising rates concentrate the compute layer's returns with its lenders.
Enterprise multi-model usage share (Menlo): Annual waves; a move under five points is survey noise. More multi-homing disperses the model layer's pricing power.
Startups' share of enterprise AI application revenue: Two annual waves, so the trend is one step; under five points is survey error. Rising startup share = value dispersing away from incumbents.
Model-layer token concentration on OpenRouter (HHI, top table): Weekly readings; moves under 0.02 in the index are table churn. A rising index means routed tokens concentrating on fewer models.
Labs buying from the training-input layer (enter bell): Four quarters; a one-point move is one vendor's single disclosure. Rising = the labs buying more from the training-input layer.
